text.title: Stakeholder Management Failure Modes
text.summary: 9 antipatterns observed across deployments. Each pairs symptom + root-cause + concrete fix. Register-rot prevention rules, decision-log pairing requirement, agent safety constraints, and AI-agent failure modes with mitigations. The rules live in 01-core-rules.xml; the agent failure modes are below.

antipattern.symptom: High-power resistor blindsides launch; team had them on Power/Interest grid as 'monitor'.
antipattern.root-cause: Grid lacked attitude column; resistor mistaken for neutral observer.
antipattern.fix: Add explicit attitude column (Supporter / Neutral / Resistor) and re-classify quarterly.

antipattern.symptom: Senior leader complains: 'nobody told me'; not on any owner's list.
antipattern.root-cause: Stakeholder row created without named owner; cadence drifted.
antipattern.fix: templates/stakeholder-lint.py rejects rows without owner + cadence; orphans must be deleted or assigned.

antipattern.symptom: All-stakeholder email triggers loud resistor reply-all; supporters disengage.
antipattern.fix: Tailor channels by attitude + power; reserve broadcasts for canonical metric rollups.

antipattern.symptom: Resistor goes silent for 3 weeks; reappears via executive sponsor block.
antipattern.root-cause: No re-engagement protocol; silence treated as acceptance.
antipattern.fix: Within 7 days of silence, schedule a 1:1 (not email) and log the outcome.

antipattern.symptom: LLM hallucinating stakeholders that "should" exist for a project type ("Compliance Officer", "Data Privacy Lead") without a source.
antipattern.root-cause: Require the model to cite an actual source — meeting notes, org chart, CODEOWNERS — before adding a row. Hallucinated stakeholders lead to wasted engagement cycles on non-existent relationships.
antipattern.fix: Apply rule cite-source-per-classification; no source, no row.

antipattern.symptom: Models defaulting to Supporter for attitude when asked "is this exec a supporter?" because of sycophantic training.
antipattern.root-cause: Force the model to mark Unknown unless evidence is cited; the stakeholder-lint.py script enforces this at commit time. Unknown attitudes must be resolved through 1:1 conversation, not LLM inference.
antipattern.fix: Apply rule attitude-column-never-blank with Unknown as the default; run templates/stakeholder-lint.py at commit.

antipattern.symptom: Power/interest classifications inferred from title alone in a matrix org where a "Senior Manager" has more real influence than a "VP".
antipattern.root-cause: Feed actual org-chart text or interview snippets rather than job titles. Title-based classification is wrong in consensus-driven and matrix orgs.
antipattern.fix: Give the classifier org-chart text or interview notes as input, never a title list.

antipattern.symptom: Cron-driven weekly stakeholder sentiment scan of Slack messages auto-escalating on mis-classified Resistor signals.
antipattern.root-cause: Queue sentiment findings for human review, never auto-escalate. A false Resistor classification triggering an escalation can damage a relationship the system was meant to protect.
antipattern.fix: Route sentiment findings to a review queue; apply rule resistor-escalation-protocol only after a human confirms.

antipattern.symptom: Long-context dumps of the full register into every agent prompt, wasting tokens and leaking PII to downstream agents.
antipattern.root-cause: Pass only the relevant slice (one quadrant, or one engagement tier) to each agent. The register as a whole is a program-management artifact, not an agent context blob.
antipattern.fix: Slice the register per agent call; apply rule scrub-pii-before-commit to anything that leaves the register.

text.reference: Lint register for rot patterns: unknown attitudes, missing owners, high-power under-engagement
